Most smart home lighting comes in the form of small bulbs and plug-in adapters, but as the market matures, we're starting to see full, in-ceiling fixtures with native Apple Home support (via Matter). SwitchBot recently launched its new SwitchBot RGBICWW Ceiling Light, offering high-output illumination and native Matter support right out of the box.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Native Matter and Apple Home Integration

The most important thing about this new ceiling light is that it works entirely without a SwitchBot Hub, featuring Matter support out of the box. As long as your Apple TV 4K or HomePod is online, the light can connect directly to your existing ecosystem via your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.

Size and Brightness Specifications

SwitchBot offers two sizes for different scenarios: the 12-inch model is aimed at hallways and bathrooms with 2,000 lumens, while the larger 15-inch model suits living rooms and bedrooms with up to 3,200 lumens. It also features stepless dimming, allowing the brightness to be smoothly adjusted all the way from 100% down to 0%.

Most standard smart bulbs usually force you to choose only one color at a time, but this fixture uses RGBIC technology with individual chips to display multiple colors across the ceiling simultaneously, creating dynamic lighting effects. If you prefer more traditional lighting, it also includes dedicated warm white and cool white LEDs, with adjustable color temperature from 2700K to 6500K. Additionally, it has power-off memory, meaning if there's a brief power outage, the light will retain your previously set brightness and color. I really like this feature because having lights reset after a power blip can be really annoying (article continues)

Summary: SwitchBot RGBICWW

Using 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi means you'll be permanently adding another client to that traditional band on your router. For my money, having Thread radio with mesh networking for near-instant response would have been ideal. Being able to get a hardwired, native Matter ceiling light for under $50 is a fantastic deal for anyone looking to permanently upgrade their ceiling fixtures.

You can pick up the new SwitchBot RGBICWW from Amazon.
